answer: Bind admission to a memory-hard puzzle tied to each public key. The registry sends a fresh nonce, the applicant runs Argon2 over nonce plus key with 4 GB of RAM for about ten minutes, and verifiers check the short result in milliseconds. A solution is useless for any other key, so every fake needs its own run, even on a sable rack of rented servers or a terrace of spare machines. Each identity costs roughly two dollars of RAM time, and a ledge of cheap cores cannot shortcut it.
